_**User**_

This works when launched from VSCode, so I reverted removal of that protocol to preserve execution monitoring. The filtering works as desired, except I'd like a custom UI to easily configure the filter criteria that is easier to use/change than the sequential popover entry method. It should live in the sidebar, only be visible when the active document is a Notebook, and have its own Filter/Clear Filter buttons.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The sidebar needs a custom filter UI for Notebooks. It should replace the sequential QuickPick with dedicated Filter and Clear Filter buttons.

WebviewView is the right choice over TreeView. It supports a form-like layout with checkboxes and buttons. Existing sidebars use TreeDataProvider, but a filter form does not fit that pattern well.

QuickPick should remain available as a fallback. The sidebar will serve as the primary filter configuration interface. It should sit in the sidebar explorer area and appear only when a Notebook is active.

The toolbar's Filter command will reveal the sidebar webview. The webview itself will host the Filter and Clear buttons. A new `notebook-cell-filter-view` webview will be added to the explorer.

The webview will display tag checkboxes, Kind radio buttons, Has Outputs and Executed dropdowns, plus Filter and Clear buttons and a match count. Draft state will sync automatically when switching notebooks or changing tags. The Filter button will apply the manager's filter, while Clear will reset it. The `set` command will be replaced by revealing the sidebar directly. I also need to verify whether package.json requires a `"type": "webview"` declaration.

Proceeding without further questions. I will check how `getAllTagsFromActiveNotebook` works and review the `package.json` commands section for filter configuration.
</details></think>

A solid plan is forming. The main design decision is between a TreeView with checkboxes and a WebviewView. The filter form needs multi-select tag support.

WebviewView is the clear winner over TreeView. It supports radio groups and dedicated Filter and Clear buttons. The plan registers a webview view in the explorer for active notebooks. A FilterWebviewProvider will render all criteria at once.

PostMessage will handle apply and clear actions. The webview will sync tags when the active notebook changes. Switching notebooks will restore that notebook's saved criteria. _**Agent (default)**_

Yes. This extension already does that for tags via overview-ruler marks on each cell’s text editor.

**How it works today**

[`src/noteAllTags/scrollbarDecorators.ts`](src/noteAllTags/scrollbarDecorators.ts) creates a `TextEditorDecorationType` with `overviewRulerColor` / `overviewRulerLane`, then for matching cells finds the cell’s `visibleTextEditors` entry and calls `setDecorations`. Those marks show up in the notebook’s scrollbar/minimap gutter.

Git diff and cell highlight helpers use the same pattern (`overviewRulerColor` in [`gitDiffProvider.ts`](src/gitDiff/gitDiffProvider.ts) and [`cellVisualHighlight.ts`](src/util/cellVisualHighlight.ts)).

**For the filter**

When a filter is active, decorate cells that pass `cellMatchesFilter` with a single decoration type (e.g. filter color on `OverviewRulerLane.Right` so it doesn’t clash with tag marks on Center). Clear those decorations on filter clear / notebook switch. Refresh on the same hooks you already use for reapply (`onDidChangeNotebookDocument`, visible editors, active notebook).

**Caveats**

- Marks only apply to cells that have a visible text editor; the existing tag decorator refreshes on `onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors` for that reason.
- This is the editor overview ruler, not a separate Explorer sidebar list. For a clickable jump list you’d add something else (e.g. a small tree of match indices).
- Collapsed non-matches won’t need marks; matching (expanded) cells are the ones you want scroll targets for.

So: yes, and the natural approach is reuse the `ScrollbarDecoratorManager` pattern, scoped to current filter match indices. I can wire that up in Agent mode if you want.

_**Agent (default)**_

Yes — that behavior is real, and the original filter plan’s “view-state only, not persisted” assumption was wrong.

**What’s going on**

1. **Collapse writes cell metadata.** The filter uses `notebook.cell.collapseCellInput` / `collapseCellOutput` ([`collapseCommands.ts`](src/notebookFilter/collapseCommands.ts)). In VS Code those commands set `metadata.inputCollapsed` / `outputCollapsed` on the cells. That can dirty the notebook; if you save (or autosave), those flags are stored in the `.ipynb` and come back on reopen.

2. **Close drops filter state without expanding.** On notebook close, startup calls `manager.forget()` — not `clear()`:

```79:83:src/notebookFilter/startup.ts
		vscode.workspace.onDidCloseNotebookDocument(notebook => {
			manager.forget(notebook);
			void manager.syncUi();
			webviewProvider.postState();
		}),
```

`forget` only removes in-memory filter tracking; it does **not** expand the cells the filter collapsed. So anything still collapsed at close stays collapsed in the document/view.

**Why it feels “auto-persisted”**

Filter state itself is not persisted (no extension workspace storage for criteria). What’s left behind is the **collapse metadata / view state** from applying the filter, then closing without clearing.

**What to change (when you want it fixed)**

- On close (and ideally on extension deactivate): if a filter is active for that notebook, call `clear()` (expand `collapsedByFilter`) instead of bare `forget()`.
- Optionally treat “closing with an active filter” the same as Clear Filter.
- Check whether filtering alone marks the notebook dirty; if yes, that’s confirmation metadata is being written.

I’m in Ask mode so I can’t apply that. Switch to Agent mode if you want the close/deactivate clear wired in.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A race condition exists where `onDidCloseNotebookDocument` may fire while the document is already closing. Expand commands could fail if the document becomes unusable. A plan is needed to handle this safely.

`clear()` should replace `forget()` when closing a document. Any remaining open notebooks with active filters must also be cleared on deactivate. `onDidCloseNotebookDocument` may be too late because the document can already be disposed. Better triggers include `onDidChangeVisibleNotebookEditors` or detecting when the last editor for a URI closes.

Executing commands on a closed document often fails silently. The manager should attempt expansion before clearing, but if that fails, cleanup must happen earlier. Tracking when the last notebook editor for a document closes via `onDidChangeVisibleNotebookEditors` is preferable to relying on `onDidCloseNotebookDocument`.

`tabGroups.onDidChangeTabs` is the most reliable trigger. It detects when a notebook tab is closed and can clear filters before the document disappears. `onDidChangeActiveNotebookEditor` is insufficient because it does not catch inactive editors.

`tabGroups.onDidChangeTabs` might fire while the document still exists, so it is not a reliable early trigger. The simpler plan is to call `clear()` inside `onDidCloseNotebookDocument` and rely on `forget()` only when expansion is unnecessary. During extension deactivation, the manager should iterate all tracked states and clear any still-open notebooks. The first concrete step is replacing `forget()` with `clear()` on document close.

`forget` should remain only for emergency state disposal after `clear`. The manager must also clear any remaining open notebooks during extension or manager teardown. `onDidChangeVisibleNotebookEditors` provides more reliable timing than `onDidCloseNotebookDocument` for detecting when the last editor for a filtered notebook disappears.

The implementation will call `manager.clear(notebook)` directly inside `onDidCloseNotebookDocument`, followed by `webviewProvider.postState()`. If the close event proves unreliable, the tab-close event can serve as a fallback. During extension or manager teardown, the remaining open notebooks will be cleared. Expanding cells on close may dirty the document again, which is the intended undo of the filter.
